The average length of stay in hospice care varies by year, population, and setting, but multiple sources converge on a range of roughly 76 to 95 days. According to NHPCO data reported by Statista, the average length of stay for Medicare hospice patients in 2022 was 95.3 days [d7]. VITAS Healthcare reports the average lifetime length of stay for Medicare decedents enrolled in hospice in 2021 was 92.1 days [d2], while other sources cite figures of 77.9 days (2018 Trella Health data) [d1] and 76.1 days overall [d5]. However, the median length of service is much shorter at just 17 days, meaning many patients enter hospice very late in their illness [d2][d3]. Average stays also differ by care setting — approximately 95 days in private homes, 109 days in nursing facilities, and 165 days in assisted living facilities — and by diagnosis, with dementia patients averaging 110 days and kidney disease patients averaging 38 days [d3][d5]. About 12–15% of patients remain in hospice for six months or more, while roughly half pass within three weeks [d4][d9].
